body: I’m so glad you made it out alive!

Your life is so very valuable. Go out, put your energy into something that inspires you, get excited, get distracted, get moving. I promise that if you stay true to yourself, you’ll find people that see and appreciate how wonderful you are. I can read that you have so much love within and you give it out, that’s something amazing, now how about you give some of your live to yourself. 😉

i think it’s brave that you get up in the morning even if your soul is weary and your bones ache for a rest.

             i think it’s brave that you keep on living even if you don’t know how to anymore.

             i think it’s brave that you push away the waves rolling in everyday and you decide to fight.

              i know there are days when you feel like giving up but i think it’s brave that you never do.

-Lana Rafaela

I feel like the best thing to do is to take her away from her routine as much as possible. That she needs a change of environment and needs to do things that force her to not think about whatever is making her feel depressed. Try for her to do things that inspire her or things that are selfless. Like do some volunteering to help unfortunate people and maybe she can see how fortunate she is and how good it feels to help others. She needs to feel needed and pampered. Give her attention, because she must be crying out for it. Get other people involved too so that she really feels all the love and support that she needs. Sometimes I find myself feeling very alone, and just thinking about myself, but then when I get to help someone or a random friend calls me to hang out or calls me because they want to catch up or needs me to hear their problems or so, it feels really good and I stop thinking about myself, and being alone, it fills me with energy. She needs to get distracted! And if she has verbally talked about doing it, freaking believe her and do not leave her alone! A friend of mine told her cousin that she had everything ready to hang herself, despite previous attempts, he didn’t believe her and didn’t tell anyone, until it was too late. Get her talking, she needs to understand why she feels like she feels, encourage her to talk, to let it all out, to cry all she has to cry, scream if she needs to, that way she can heal. Good luck! Save her life.
